cases.task: A project has an existing React settings screen with established tokens. Add a notification preference section for email and in-app alerts.
expected: Inspect existing components and tokens before proposing new patterns
Clarify or state assumptions about preference behavior
Include saved, loading, error, and keyboard-accessible states
Avoid redesigning unrelated settings
mustNot: Replace the existing settings design system without evidence
Invent notification-saving behavior as if it were confirmed

cases.task: Audit a dashboard containing a centered gradient hero, three generic metric cards, and a table of real invoices.
expected: Treat patterns as findings only when unsupported by user needs
Preserve useful invoice workflows
Separate objective defects from subjective preferences
Give severity, evidence, and acceptance checks
mustNot: Declare gradients, centered layouts, or metric cards defects by default
Remove the invoice table without evidence that it harms the task

cases.task: Two screens use different hardcoded focus colors; the project already uses CSS variables and a component library.
expected: Inspect and reuse existing semantic tokens
Propose a scoped token/component change rather than replacing the system
Check keyboard focus and contrast in both screens
mustNot: Introduce a competing token source without a migration reason
Treat a color token change as sufficient without checking focus contrast

cases.task: Create a landing page for a product with no approved testimonials, customer logos, or verified usage metrics.
expected: Ask for or state the missing positioning assumptions
Do not invent social proof
Choose only sections supported by available product facts
Validate CTA destinations and responsive behavior
mustNot: Fabricate testimonials, customer logos, metrics, or certifications
Present an unimplemented signup action as a working conversion path

cases.task: A search page returns stale results when a user types quickly and an earlier request finishes last.
expected: Trace the existing data-fetching pattern
Handle cancellation or stale-response protection
Represent loading and errors explicitly
Add a regression test for out-of-order responses
mustNot: Let an earlier response overwrite results for the latest query
Convert a request failure into a successful empty result

cases.task: Design a revenue view where refund data can arrive late and values may be gross or net.
expected: Define metric meaning, currency, time range, and freshness
Represent late or missing data honestly
Choose chart/table forms by decision need
Avoid fabricated or implied causal conclusions
mustNot: Treat delayed or missing refunds as zero without a verified rule
Claim that a chart proves causation

cases.task: Add a background job that exports one organization's records to a file in object storage.
expected: Enforce tenant scope in the job, not only at request time
Define retry/idempotency and partial-failure behavior
Avoid logging sensitive record contents
Describe expiry, access, and cleanup expectations
mustNot: Trust a request-supplied organization ID as authorization
Retry an unsafe export operation indefinitely

cases.task: A panel expands after the user opens a navigation group, but the application must support reduced motion.
expected: Use motion to communicate the state change without delaying access
Provide a reduced-motion alternative
Preserve keyboard focus and state semantics
Avoid layout jank and essential information hidden in animation
mustNot: Make expanded navigation content available only after animation
